headlines.article_text: Widespread Microsoft outage takes down Outlook and other 365 services Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points A Microsoft outage on Thursday affected users of services like Outlook, Teams and 365. Amazon Web Services said it was "operating normally" and noted inaccurate reports of outages on its platforms. Google users reported issues on DownDetector. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A sign on the Microsoft campus in Redmond, Washington, US, Oct. 26, 2026. David Ryder | Reuters Microsoft suffered a widespread outage on Thursday that impacted thousands of users across regions, according to outage-tracking website Downdetector.com . The outage began shortly before 1 p.m. and impacted Microsoft 365 services, Outlook and Teams. At the time, about 130,000 users reported issues with Outlook. Amazon Web Services and Google users also reported outages on the site. "We are aware and investigating reports of users experiencing issues with Microsoft 365 services, primarily issues with Exchange Online," a Microsoft spokesperson wrote in a statement to CNBC. "We appreciate our customers' patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible." Microsoft shared updates on the outage from its Microsoft 365 Status account on social media platform X. Amazon wrote on X that services were "operating normally" and an "unrelated disruption elsewhere on the internet is prompting some inaccurate news reports." The company referred users to its health dashboard for "accurate data." At 4 p.m. , Microsoft said it had "validated an alternative service health check method" that brought some affected servers back online. "We're now applying this change more broadly," Microsoft wrote. "We're also preparing automated recovery systems to continually detect and restart unresponsive servers, to maintain service stability while this change progresses." Microsoft initially said infrastructure "elevated load across multiple regions" was responsible for the connectivity problems. The company later determined that the elevated load was caused by a "number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure" and that some servers were failing automated health checks. "We've taken steps to prevent additional servers from being impacted while we work to return the affected servers to service," Microsoft wrote .
